title: Define review contacts and escalation fallback for PRD acceptance
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Establish a lightweight, auditable contact and escalation pattern for PRD review and acceptance across Eng/Design/Legal. Goal: reduce last-minute blockers by clarifying who owns signoff for each acceptance area, what acceptable evidence looks like, and a defined fallback escalation path when primary owners are unavailable. This ticket collects contacts, creates a short runbook, and pilots the flow on the current Structured Output PRD slice.
background: Recent PRD reviews have encountered repeated delays when reviewers (tech leads, design lead, or legal reviewer) are out of cycle. This causes scope slip and unplanned rollbacks. We need a repeatable, low-friction process that (1) defines per-acceptance-area owners, (2) enumerates required artifacts for signoff, and (3) provides a 24–72h fallback ladder so product can progress without blocking releases.
scope:
- Produce a one-page runbook and ownership table for PRD acceptance lanes (API/SDK compatibility, UX/Design, Security/Legal, SLO/Telemetry).
- Pilot the runbook for the Structured Output PRD slice and capture learnings.
- Create links and templates for required artifacts (design spec checklist, infra test matrix, legal dataflow signoff).
out_of_scope:
- Full automation of the signoff process (tooling integrations).
- Changes to org-level RACI outside product/eng/design/legal for this pilot.
acceptance_criteria: One-page runbook published in Confluence with clear contact table for each acceptance lane
Per-lane artifact checklist (minimum evidence) attached to the PRD template
Fallback ladder defined with two alternates per lane and SLA for response times (24h primary, 48–72h fallback)
Pilot executed for Structured Output PRD: at least one signoff completed via the new flow and retrospective notes captured
Runbook reviewed and acknowledged by Eng Director, Head of Design, and Legal Counsel
